item.title: Local coach on need for sports facilities for young people
item.description: A local volunteer has highlighted the importance of making sure that young people continue to play sports as they get older. That’s according to Colm Connolly, an underage coach with Clones GAA. He highlighted that in rural areas, facilities are essential to keeping young people involved with sport. Advertisement It comes as the club has outlined ambitious plans to renovate and expand its facilities. item.title: All roads lead to Croke Park for Knockbride
item.description: All roads lead to Croke Park this weekend as Knockbride take on Caltra of Galway. Tomorrow at 2pm Knockbride will face the Galway side in the All Ireland ladies intermediate final. It will be a first time for the club not only being in an All Ireland final but also in Croke Park. Advertisement The game will be live on Northern Sound with thanks to The Bridge Tavern Canningstown. Proprietor of the local bar, Adrian Rodgers says excitement is building as all roads lead for Croker.

item.title: Local member of An Garda Síochana encourages property marking
item.description: A local member of An Garda Síochana is calling on people across the region to have their valuables security marked. Sergeant Joe Glackin who is the Crime Prevention Officer for Cavan and Monaghan is encouraging locals to get their property marked. He said members of the public who have a quad, bicycle, trailer, strimmer or any other valuable item should get them marked with their Eircode. item.title: Man in his 70s attacked in Keady home
item.description: Detectives in Newry are investigating the attempted murder of an older man at his Keady home on Thursday night, 11th December. At around 7.35pm, it was reported that six masked men armed with bats entered the living room of the man’s home on the Clay Road. The intruders proceeded to attack the man, who is aged in his 70s, with the bats continuing the assault as he lay on the floor. item.title: New Ballybay Fire Station to open early 2026
item.description: The new Ballybay Fire Station will be a highly important development for not only the town but the wider area. That's according to Cathaoirleach of the Ballybay-Clones Municipal District Sinead Flynn. Despite a long period of construction, it is hoped that the new facility will be open during the first quarter of 2026.
